# recipe-box

## Project overview

Web app where families save, organize and share recipes.

## Language policy

- Code, comments, docs and commit messages: English.
- Replies to the user: English.

## Tech stack

Uses: TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js, pnpm, PostgreSQL, Vitest, next-intl.

- Use the Node.js version pinned in `.nvmrc` or in the `engines` field of package.json, never whatever version is installed globally. Why: Node.js versions differ in behavior and break native dependencies.
- Use pnpm for every install and script. Never run npm or yarn. Why: Mixing package managers creates conflicting lockfiles.

## Commands

- Dev: `pnpm dev`
- Test: `pnpm test`

## Code style

- App locales: en (default) and it. Translate new text into every locale yourself.

## Other rules

- Keep the changelog in `CHANGELOG.md`. Add an entry for every user-visible change. Why: Users read the changelog, not the git log.

## Safety rules

- Never edit, skip or delete an existing test to make it pass. Fix the code, or stop and ask. Why: A passing test suite is only meaningful if the tests stay honest.
- Keep secrets in `.env`, which stays in `.gitignore`; never hardcode or commit them, and do not read `.env` files. When you add a variable, add its name with a placeholder value to `.env.example`. Why: A committed secret stays in git history and has to be rotated.

## Further reading

- Before adding a feature, read docs/PRODUCT.md.
- Before adding a dependency or changing how the app is structured, read docs/agents/architecture.md.
- Before writing code, read docs/agents/style.md.
- Before adding or changing user-facing text, read docs/agents/i18n.md.
- Before writing or changing tests, read docs/agents/testing.md.
- Before committing or opening a pull request, read docs/agents/git.md.
- Before starting a task, read docs/agents/workflow.md.
- For code review rules, read docs/agents/code-review.md.
